newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin wants Mobutu property returned to his country.
newsitem.headline: Jospin wants Mobutu property returned to his country.

text.p: French Socialist opposition leader Lionel Jospin said on Tuesday that fallen Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko's considerable assets abroad should be handed back to his country and his people.

"Since we know there are a certain amount of assets in several countries which belong to him privately, I think the countries which have these assets in their banking systems should find a way to hand these back to the Zairean state and people," he told a political rally in Montpellier, southern France.

His comment coincided with a front-page cartoon in the satirical weekly Le Canard Enchaine showing a Swiss banker saying on the telephone: "Sorry, we only allow serving dictators to have access to their bank accounts."

Jospin expressed wariness about the democratic intentions of the country's new leader, Laurent Desire Kabila, and suggested the international community should apply pressure to ensure free elections were held in the troubled African country.
Jospin said France should revise its African policy which he said was based on "overly personal" relations between Paris and some African leaders.
The Socialist leader has no influence on French foreign policy but would be in charge of it if the left-wing coalition he now leads were to win the country's May 25-June 1 general election.

France's Socialists have been criticised in the past for assailing the Paris government's African policies, often based on supporting dictators, when the Socialists were in opposition but in leaving such policies unchanged when they were in power.
